messages.text:
"Сделаем Avto-M Driller HDD 2.0 не просто аркадой с буровой, а полноценным игровым симулятором работы бригады ГНБ — с реалистичной площадкой, персонажами, подземным разрезом, выбором инструмента и последствиями решений оператора.

Я изучил рекомендации производителей бурового оборудования и материалы по технологии ГНБ. Важный момент: успех бурения зависит не только от скорости установки, но и от траектории пилотной скважины, контроля положения головки, свойств бурового раствора, состояния штанг и правильного расширения скважины перед протяжкой коммуникации.@COMMENT_BODY@#x20;

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.ditchwitch.com&sz=32)

Ditch Witch+3



## Как будет устроена новая игра

[Установка горизонтально-направленного бурения Vermeer D24 — ГНБ нового поколения](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/fONJhCTmOLTXuNgd-k0IsM1PGG9mFiHilWVfMCD7_3MxId-kq4ZAHJSs_MZezDg2p2OYsiobd1XvgHVLmibN_LgyUK-633KsJY_qcnunHyMh7yugkv8eVUpgnHqjWnDAkET7dXBxEhH69PhJABxzDBK4iJdpwenpBRWtt9Y4PEo?purpose=inline)

1\. Реалистичная строительная площадка

Буровая установка, оператор, локаторщик, помощник, буровые штанги, смесительная установка, шланги, ограждения, автомобиль снабжения и рабочая зона. Персонажи будут участвовать в процессе, а не просто стоять декорацией.

[How’s the market of the HDD will be in 2024?](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/kcKCxf5PYCzPrdaEYTmfe0PAKrS1hZBRjdO6IAAARE8z0W_VKkrceXpr-crAd1TDz548rU2HXOaRQb03VKmTVgI2KbrnPoIoZfbt6WiYYlBDgLDbeoW8_phd0QQbAj7dSou38J9BJZ3Lwi9SHq92ftHumBwPA0SmZI4AwH3KMkc?purpose=inline)

2\. Настоящий подземный разрез

Слои грунта, проектная траектория, глубина буровой головки, существующие кабели и трубы. Будет видно, куда фактически идёт скважина и насколько она отклоняется от проекта.

[Make Drilling More Precise With Subsite’s Marksman… | Dig Different](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/o2S2ZDyUD9xvfP6NU_3Ctoe2p-vfNL2RCO5nwfdP3Bu6wp2D24jPs8lCY1g0Gi1qUmjwwQlidBFBtfTvD5-G5piblADvkdUuYlK1aUAVw-A8Vv1Thmg7M_fp0cgu46W5GlyG_eJsvvm55gUzB0ouMIhQl0LTVmIIvGSbkqkkPSU?purpose=inline)

3\. Бригада с индивидуальными бонусами

Оператор повышает производительность и точность управления, локаторщик улучшает контроль траектории, специалист по раствору снижает риск проблем с промывкой, механик сокращает простои.

## Реалистичная последовательность работ

В игре будет пять основных этапов:

1\. Подготовка объекта

Проверка коммуникаций, разметка трассы, выбор входной и выходной точек, подготовка оборудования.

2\. Пилотное бурение

Подача и вращение штанг, управление головкой, контроль глубины, уклона и положения локаторщиком.

3\. Контроль бурового раствора

Подача раствора, удаление выбуренной породы, контроль давления и риска выхода раствора на поверхность.

4\. Расширение скважины

Выбор подходящего расширителя с учётом диаметра прокладываемой коммуникации и грунта.

5\. Протяжка и сдача объекта

Подключение вертлюга, протяжка трубы или кабеля, контроль усилия, проверка результата и расчёт прибыли.

Все эти этапы соответствуют общей технологии ГНБ; конкретные параметры должны зависеть от техники, грунта и проекта.@COMMENT_BODY@#x20;

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.fws.gov&sz=32)

Служба рыб и дикой природы США+2



## Персонажи и развитие бригады

Предлагаю систему найма и прокачки специалистов:

- Оператор ГНБ — скорость проходки, точность и снижение перегрузок.
- Локаторщик — точность определения положения головки и раннее обнаружение отклонений.
- Специалист по буровым растворам — расход материалов, очистка скважины и риск осложнений.
- Механик — надёжность установки, ремонт и время простоя.
- Бригадир — организация работ, скорость выполнения заказа и премия за качество.

У каждого будут уровень опыта, зарплата, навыки и индивидуальные бонусы. Сильная бригада будет стоить дороже, но сможет брать более сложные и прибыльные заказы.

Важный момент: сейчас мне не удалось вызвать инструмент, необходимый для создания и проверки обновлённого файла игры. Поэтому новую версию 2.0 я
"

content.text:
Static HTML game. Need to create index.html. It can reference local JS/CSS files. Let's plan the game architecture.

The user asks a big concept. Since message truncated, we should implement a full game demonstrating the described features. Most important: playable, polished, mobile-friendly, Russian UI.

Design:

Game: "Avto-M Driller HDD 2.0" — a crew-based HDD (horizontal directional drilling) simulator.

Core gameplay loop:
- Choose a contract (order): pipe diameter, length, soil, obstacles, payout, difficulty.
- Prepare site: crew assignment? Maybe roster/hire screen.
- Pilot bore: steer the drill head through underground cross-section avoiding utilities, following design path. Controls: thrust/rotation, steering (pitch), mud flow. Locator readings.
- Mud control: pressure, flow, returns; risk of frac-out.
- Reaming: choose reamer diameter matching product + soil; pass along bore.
- Pullback: attach product, pull with force limits.
- Settlement: profit, crew XP, results.

Needs 5 stages, 5 crew roles with bonuses, tool selection, consequences. Underground cross-section with layers, existing utilities, actual vs design path.

Implementation: single-page canvas game with UI overlay. Use Canvas 2D. Responsive layout: wide desktop shows site view left/top, cross-section right/bottom, HUD. Mobile portrait stacks.

Game architecture in JS modules:
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js (state, loop)
- src/world.js (contracts, crew, soils, tools, utilities)
- src/render.js (canvas drawing)
- src/ui.js

Could do single app.js to simplify. But clean modules better for maintainability.

Let me think through mechanics concretely so the game is actually fun and coherent.

Physics model along the bore path:
- 2D cross-section with x = horizontal distance (m), y = depth (m).
- Drill head position (x, depth), heading angle (pitch) in degrees; drill string advances when thrust applied, rotation speed; steering changes pitch based on rotation + steering input. In real HDD, steering achieved by orienting bent sub and thrusting without rotation.
- Simplify: player controls thrust (0-100), rotation (0-100), steering up/down (-1..1). Steering effectiveness only when rotation is low (sliding), which teaches real technique. But too complex for casual play? It's a simulator — nice.
- Design path displayed. Deviation accumulates; locator gives depth/pitch readings with noise depending on locator skill. If head crosses utility safety zone → strike → damage/fail. If depth too shallow near end → exit point mismatch. Must reach exit target within tolerance.
- Mud: flow and pressure; cuttings removal. Keep pressure within window based on depth/soil; too high → frac-out risk; too low → stuck. Mud quality/consumption. Pump controls.
- Rods: each 3m rod; auto rod addition pauses progress. Rod condition / torque. If thrust too high with rotation → rod fatigue/damage.
- Reaming: choose reamer diameter (e.g., product OD × 1.25–1.5). Pass back along path. Tool load depends on soil and diameter. Wrong size → pullback too tight or excessive force.
- Pullback: attach swivel, pull force gauge; keep below limit; if too high, risk pipe damage. Use mud.
- Timing and scoring: time, deviation, cost, quality, profit.

Maybe simplify stages into a flow:

Stage 1 PREP: interactive checklist: scan utilities (click markers), set entry/exit points, mud mix ratio selection, choose reamer. Each choice affects outcome. Use crew assignments.

Stage 2 PILOT: real-time steering canvas. Goal reach exit pit at target depth. Utilities visible on site map (preview). Locator signal gives current depth/pitch with error. Mud pressure managed automatically? Add sliders for thrust/rotation; mud auto but pressure rises with thrust. Events: frac-out, utility strike, rod fatigue, stuck.

Stage 3 MUD/reaming combined? User wants 5 distinct stages. We can have:
- Stage 3 Ream: select reamer from options (diameter, type: fly cutter, barrel reamer, hole opener) then run reaming pass; a pass meter and load. Player adjusts mud flow and pull force.
- Stage 4 Pullback: attach product, pull, keep force under limit by mud control.
- Stage 5 Handover: results, payment, crew XP, next contract.

But user listed mud as stage 3 and reaming as 4, pullback 5. Could combine mud control into pilot and reaming as active mechanics, but show five stage timeline where mud control is its own segment after pilot (circulation/cleaning). Maybe after pilot, "промывка/очистка скважины" mini-stage: adjust flow to remove cuttings, then reaming, then pullback. That's 5: Prep, Pilot, Mud/Circulation, Reaming, Pullback+Handover.

Simplify mud: In "Промывка" stage player picks/controls pump flow for a short time to clean hole; an animation of cuttings. Quality affects reaming/pullback. Or during pilot, mud control is active with pressure gauge; stage 3 involves conditioning the hole: set flow and viscosity additive dose.

I think a well-crafted game with 4 interactive scenes (Prep checklist, Pilot, Ream, Pullback) plus a mud conditioning scene is plenty.

Crew:
- 5 roles, 3 candidates each? Hiring with salaries and levels. Maybe roster of 5 default crew plus hiring candidate pool per contract. To keep scope manageable: 5 roles, each with 3 selectable specialists (different cost/skill/bonus), and XP/leveling over contracts. Persist via localStorage.

Bonuses:
- Operator: thrust control precision (steering response/stability), reduces rod wear.
- Locator: reduces signal noise, earlier deviation warnings, wider utility detection.
- Mud tech: lower mud consumption, wider safe pressure window, faster cuttings removal.
- Mechanic: reduces breakdown chance, faster rig repair, lower fuel cost.
- Foreman: time bonus, payout bonus, fewer random events.

Site: characters animated at positions, with role labels; on events they animate/reply in radio log. Nice visuals: isometric-ish side view? We can render site in a stylized 2.5D side elevation: rig on left, pit, grass, fence, truck, mixing unit, crew figures. Underground cross-section below with soil layers and utilities. This can all be one canvas: top ground line ~35% height, underground below. On desktop, cross-section occupies lower 65%. Good.

Rendering style: clean vector art with gradients, dark navy HUD panels, orange accents (drilling industry). Use canvas for scene, HTML/CSS for HUD/buttons. Character figures drawn as simple workers with helmets; animate walking, arm gestures, drill movement, mud particles.

Interaction:
- Pilot stage: on-screen controls (HTML buttons/sliders or custom touch pads): "Подача" throttle (0-100), "Вращение" (0-100), steering up/down buttons. Keyboard: W/S or arrows steer, A/D thrust? Standard: ↑/↓ steering, +/− thrust, hold Space rotation? Need simple. Use sliders + hold buttons for mobile.
- We can design steering: tap/hold Up/Down to change target pitch; the drill follows. Rotation slider; sliding (rotation 0) gives faster steering. Thrust slider advances. On mobile, big buttons: "ВВЕРХ", "ВНИЗ", plus throttle +/-? Hmm.

Alternative simplified control: throttle slider on left vertical, steering left/right (up/down depth) with two buttons, rotation auto when thrust. For a game, arcade steering by holding up/down while drill advances is more accessible. Add "режим": rotation high = straight, low = steer. Auto rotation unless steering pressed; if player steers while rotation high, poor response and rod stress. Show indicator "Скольжение / Вращение".

Let me define pilot mechanics:
- Holding "Подача" (thrust) increases advance speed up to max; drag slider sets target thrust 0..100.
- Drill advances continuously when thrust > 0 at speed = thrust/100 * maxRate (maxRate ~0.55 m/s game time; 150m bore = ~4.5 min; too long). Use accelerated scale: each rod 3m added in ~1.2s at full thrust. MaxRate 2.5 m/s. 120m in ~48s at full. Good.
- Steering: hold Up/Down adjusts pitch at rate depending on rotation. If rotation > 60%, steering effectiveness 20%; if rotation < 30%, full. Player can toggle rotation with "Вращение" toggle. Auto: rotation on by default, turn off to steer. Simulator nuance.
- Depth changes = sin(pitch) * ds. Design path is polyline; cap deviation.
- Utility strike if within clearance (0.4m). Utilities drawn with depth and x ranges. There are 2-3 per site.
- Exit target: must reach x_end with depth target ±1.5m. If overshoot, fail/repair time.
- Exit early: if within zone at end → success.
- Frac-out: if mud pressure too high while shallow (<3m depth) and flow high, chance event; add a mud pressure slider too? That's 3 controls + steer. Maybe mud auto-adjusted with "pressure" slider. Could make mud a separate stage. During pilot, mud is automatic; a gauge shows pressure with safe band dependent on depth; player can adjust pump with a small slider. Too much; keep mud automatic during pilot but affected by crew. Stage 3 gives mud interaction. That's cleaner.

- Rod wear: if thrust > 85 for long, fatigue increases; mechanic skill mitigates. At wear threshold event "замена штанги" pause.

Stage timeline bar with stage names; money/cost ticking.

Prep stage:
- Checklist: 
  1) "Проверить коммуникации" — click 3 utility markers on map to scan, reveals depths; if skipped, locator accuracy during pilot suffers (unknown utility).
  2) "Разметить трассу" — drag entry/exit markers? Simpler: choose entry point among 3 (left positions) and exit among 3; path design appears. Different options affect length/soil/payout. Click markers on the map.
  3) "Приготовить раствор" — choose mix: бентонит / полимер / комбинированный — affects pressure window/cost by soil.
  4) "Подобрать расширитель" — choose from 3 diameters/types based on product OD; cost and risk.
  5) "Проверить установку" — mechanic check? maybe crew assignment already.
- Each check gives cost/time; player must complete mandatory ones before "Начать пилотное бурение". Consequences: skipping utility scan = unknown utilities and higher strike risk.

Crew screen at start: 5 roles with candidate selection. Maybe first run default crew; "Бригада" panel accessible between contracts, hire/upgrade with money.

For a single playable demo, include:
- Start screen with game title, brief instructions, "Начать смену".
- Contract selection (3 contracts with difficulty, length, diameter, soil, payout).
- Crew assignment screen (choose one per role from 2-3 candidates; budget? salaries deducted per job).
- Prep stage interactive checklist.
- Pilot.
- Mud conditioning.
- Reaming.
- Pullback.
- Results.

Persistence: localStorage for money, crew XP, completed contracts.

That's a large build but doable. Need good visuals and testing. Let's plan file structure:

index.html — app shell with screens.
styles.css — full responsive UI.
src/data.js — soils, contracts, crew, reamers, mud mixes, utilities.
src/state.js — game state creation, save/load, economy.
src/render.js — canvas scenes: site + cross-section, pilot, ream, pullback visuals.
src/game.js — loop, mechanics, stage transitions.
src/ui.js — DOM binding, screens.
src/main.js — bootstrap.

Maybe simpler: app.js ~2000 lines. But maintainable modules preferred.

Canvas rendering details:
- Canvas fills a stage area with aspect ratio; use devicePixelRatio scaling and ResizeObserver.
- World coordinates: x from 0..contract.length+40 m; mapping to screen. For site view, show entire site (fixed), cross-section scaled.
- Sky gradient, distant hills, grass field, road, fence.
- Rig: orange Vermeer-like tracked rig at entry; mast angled; cabin; drill string entering ground. Draw rods along path? Actual bore path drawn as dark tube with dashed design line; head with sonde.
- Characters: operator in cab? Draw 4-5 figures: operator at rig console (next to rig), locator walking ahead with receiver, mud tech at mixing tank, foreman with tablet, mechanic near truck. Animate subtle bobbing; highlight active worker per stage.
- Mixing unit, water tank, hose, rods rack, truck, excavator maybe, safety fence, cones, port-a-john.
- Underground: layered soil bands (topsoil, clay, sand, gravel, rock), random pebbles, design path dashed cyan, actual bore orange, utilities with colors and labels, entry/exit pits.
- Depth grid with labels every 2m.


```
 thrust = feedHeld||autoFeed ? (auto?0.55:1) : 0
 rotation = rotOn ? 1 : 0

 pitch += steering * 28deg/s * steerEff * dt * operatorSkillFactor
```

content.text:
Now render.js. This is the biggest craft part. Let's write in chunks.

Structure:

```js
import { prepareContract, UTILITY_TYPES, SOILS } from './data.js';
import { clamp, lerp, seeded } from './util.js';

export class Renderer {
  constructor(canvas) { ... }
  setContract(contract) { ... texture ... }
  resize()
  draw(game, t, opts={})
  ...
}
```

Game state fields expected:
- stage, contract (prepared), design, utilities (with revealed flags on job.utilityState? let's store `job.utilities` copies with `revealed`, `detected`)
- head, path, prep, crew (members), stats
- stageData: `mud` {flow, pressure, cleaned, ...}, `ream` {progress, load, ...}, `pull` {...}
- fx {scan, frac, toastShake}
- `demo` optional.

We'll make renderer robust.

Resize:
```js
resize() {
 const r=this.canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
 if(!r.width||!r.height) return false;
 const dpr=Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio||1, 2);
 if (this.w!==r.width||this.h!==r.height||this.dpr!==dpr) { ... }
 this.w=r.width; this.h=r.height;
 return true;
}
```

View:
```js
computeView(game) {
 const c=game.contract;
 const narrow=this.w<620;
 const full=game.stage==='prep'||game.stage==='mud'||game.stage==='results'||this.demo;
 let x0,x1, groundFrac;
 if(full){ x0 = narrow?-13:-24; x1 = c.length + (narrow?12:20); groundFrac = narrow?0.28:0.30; }
 else {
   let focus = game.head?.x || 0;
   if(game.stage==='ream') focus = ... ; if pull ...
   const vw = narrow?32:58;
   let cx = clamp(focus + vw*0.08, -14+vw*0.45, c.length+10-vw*0.55)? 
```
Need simpler:
```
x0 = focus - vw*0.42;
x0 = clamp(x0, -24, Math.max(-24, c.length+12-vw));
```
But if length 85 and vw 58, max x0=39; at start focus 0 → -24.4 clamped -24. fine. At exit focus 85 → 60.8 → clamped 39, so exit at right edge (39+58=97). Good.
For narrow vw 32: max x0=65; start -20; follow.

groundY = h*(full?0.30:0.32).
Visible depth: full = maxDepth+3.2, follow = narrow?9.5:9.0. sy = (h-groundY-14)/depth. For h=400, ground 128, sy=28.6. Good. Horizontal: w/(x1-x0).
Return view.

However for full mobile: h maybe 330, ground 105, depth 9, sy=23.4; scale x=390/(85+25)=3.5. Extreme exaggeration 6.7x. Visual still readable as schematic. Pipes circles become ellipses if using sy for radius while x width uses sx; utility circle radius should be horizontal in x units? In side elevation, a circular pipe cross-section should be a circle in screen px (using sy) since it's perpendicular. Draw circle radius = size/2*sy maybe. Fine.

Draw sky:
```
const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,gy); stops #07131d, #143041, #3f5a5e, #c98a4c? 
```
Golden hour: top #0b1b28 → #23485a → #7d7a63 → #e3a45f near ground. But the underground dark. Surface warm.
Sun at (w*0.78, gy*0.28) radial gradient.

Hills: fill polygons using sine; colors #16303b, #1c3b40 with slight orange rim.

Clouds: draw 3 soft ellipses with low alpha, positions based on time? Static.

Ground strip: green-brown band 0-? The topsoil layer begins underground. At surface draw 4px grass line #4a5c3a, and site gravel pad from x=-16 to 4.

Underground background first fill #1b1713.

Layers: for each layer top..bottom; wavy boundary. Draw path across full width:
```
for x from -20 to w step 40, y = worldY(layer.top) + sin((x/w)*6 + i)*1.2
```
Actually boundary should be consistent with world x; use screen x. Fill from boundary to next. Add subtle gradient per layer? Use solid + overlay gradient. Draw layer name at left or right edge? Add small labels along left side in full view: e.g., "СУГЛИНОК" vertical? Maybe not.

Texture: precomputed pebbles in world coords. Set on setContract:
```js
const rnd=seeded(seed)
for i<320: x = rnd()*length, d = rnd()* (maxDepth+4); determine layer color? use rgba light/dark.
```
Store {x,d,size,type}. Draw if in view. Pebbles color based on depth layer via contract.layers lookup. Draw small rounded rect/circle, alpha .25.
Also root/stone shapes for rock.

Grid: vertical lines at multiples of 10m; labels bottom? Draw vertical lines from ground to bottom with alpha .06; labels at top of underground? On ground line small "20 м". Horizontal depth lines every 2m with label on left "2 м" (dark chip). On narrow, every 2m maybe clutter; use 2m, small.

Utilities:
Only draw if `game.utilityVisible(u)`? Renderer can check `u.revealed`. Job copies utilities with `revealed`. For hero demo all revealed.

For each utility within view:
- if not revealed: maybe if detected, draw pulsing hazard marker; else skip.
- draw vertical hazard band: x ± (clearance horizontal? screen 3px), from surface to depth+2? Use gradient red alpha. Actually draw a thin dashed vertical line from surface to bottom at u.x, plus surface diamond. Hazard clearance ellipse around pipe.
- pipe: circle radius = max(5, u.size/2 * sy * 1.6) (exaggerate size), fill dark casing ring + color center. Ellipse with ry=size/2*sy maybe.
- clearance ellipse dashed: rx = max(10, u.clearance* sx * 2?) Hmm horizontal clearance in world x is small; player passes through at an x. The hazard zone is a vertical band of width (clearance*2 in x) not an ellipse. Draw a translucent vertical band from u.x-clearance to u.x+clearance from ground to depth+2, and a circle around pipe radius clearance in screen sy. This communicates.
- label chip near pipe: colored border, text with depth. Clamp to canvas.
- surface marker diamond and vertical dashed line.
- if utility is close to head x (<12m), draw pulsing.

Design:
- convert points to screen.
- dashed line cyan, lineWidth 1.5, dash [7,7], alpha .85.
- Add depth target markers? Draw small arrows every 15m with "проект".
- Target at exit: bullseye at (exitX, exitDepth) with radius 12, dashed circle; depth tolerance band rectangle/ellipse.

Bore:
- path array; for stages pilot, path; for ream/pull full path. Draw smooth polyline (lineJoin round).
- outer #0a0c0d width 10; inner #3a2b1f width 7? Then orange line width 3.2 with glow. Add rod ticks every 3m along path: compute along path by distance, draw perpendicular small line 5px.
- Moving mud dots: every 12px, dot with alpha pulse based on time and index. Expensive but fine; limit.

Actually draw bore before design? Design should remain visible as dashed overlay maybe on top. Draw design first, then bore, then design dashed again? Keep design on top with low alpha to compare. Draw design beneath, bore above; deviation visible.

Rig/equipment drawn after underground so overlap at surface. Entry pit should be drawn before rig.

Pits:
Entry pit at x=0: trapezoid from x-2.2 to x+2.2 at ground, down 1.3m, fill #100c09, sides orange-ish. Exit pit at length similarly.
Draw casing/liner? no.

Equipment:
Draw only if visible x range. `drawRig(view, entryX)`; `drawTank`, etc. For narrow hide some.

Rig drawing in screen coords with `s = narrow?0.74:1`; anchor around worldX(-4.5), groundY. Let's design dimensions:
- base tracks width 150*s height 26*s, at y=0.
- body from -60..+50 x, -60..-20 y, orange.
- cab from +10..+48, -95..-58 with glass.
- mast pivot at -10,-58; tip near entry pit at +80? Mast rotated ~35°, length 130*s. Use line with thick stroke and rails. Carriage at 60% with drill string.
- Since entry pit at worldX(0), anchor x = worldX(-4) and mast tip should reach worldX(0), which is ~4m* sx (at full 3.5px/m = 14px mobile; wide 8px/m=32px). Mast mostly vertical? Real rig mast is angled ~20° from horizontal? HDD rigs have mast at ~15-20° from horizontal, long. To span from anchor to entry, draw mast leaning right 30° from vertical? Hmm. A Vermeer D24 has a long angled mast from low rear to high front? Actually mast angled downward toward ground entry, ~20° above horizontal. In side view, rig body horizontal, mast at 20-30° pointing down to entry pit. Let’s draw mast from top-left of body (x=-45,y=-85) to entry (x=+55, y=-10), a long diagonal. That looks like a drill rig. Carriage moves along it.

Draw mast as two parallel thick lines (dark) with orange edges; hydraulic cylinder. Drill string from carriage down along mast into pit.

At pilot start with x small, bore starts at entry.

Truck/mud tank etc.

Workers drawn after equipment.

Locator at surface above head with receiver and dashed line to head: draw only pilot.

Hero demo uses same.

Mud FX:
- Pumping: particles at exit pit rising and falling. Deterministic: for i 0..14, phase=(t*1.3+i*.37)%1; x=exitX+sin(phase*pi)*2; y=ground - sin(phase*pi)*20*(0.4+rand) ; color #7dd3a7 alpha. Draw circles.
- In mud stage, also a hose from tank to rig.
- Frac fountain: if fx.frac>0, big plume at x (head.x or exit) with particles.

Ream visual:
- tool progress from exit (0) to entry (1). Use path point at reversed distance. Draw reamer barrel: circle radius 16 + ratio*4, orange/steel, teeth triangles around, rotate based on time. Mud spray.
- draw a tow line from reamer toward exit/rig? Draw swivel and rods.
- In pull stage: leading end at path position reversed; product pipe drawn along path behind (from exit to leading). Draw thick dark pipe with blue stripe. At leading end, swivel.
- At entry, product emerges? Since leading moves toward entry, when progress ~100 it reaches entry pit.

Camera focus: computed by job method or renderer:
```js
if ream: f = exitX - progress*(exitX)
if pull same
```
Actually set focus = head? Use job.cameraTarget maybe. Job sets `this.camFocus` each update. Simpler renderer computes.

Title hero: demo object stage 'prep', full view, head path demo. Full view.

Let's write render.js in chunks.

Chunk 1: imports, class, resize, view, draw skeleton, helpers, sky, hills, ground, layers, grid.
Created file successfully: src/render.js

Now R2: utilities, design, bore, pits. Need job utilities with revealed flags. Renderer assumes game.utilities each has revealed. In demo set revealed true.

`isRevealed(u, game)`: u.revealed !== false. Job sets booleans. If unknown but detected maybe `u.detected`. Draw "?" hazard.

Utility pipe circles: use X(u.x), Y(u.depth); r = max(5, u.size*this.v.sy*0.8). Draw outer dark ring, color ring, inner dark. Clearance ellipse with rx = max(10, 0.55*sx?) Since x clearance measured in meters along path; use screen px: clearanceX = u.clearance * sx (world meters horizontally). At full sx ~8 → 5px, too thin. Exaggerate: max(14, u.clearance*sx). Hazard band width 2*max(14,...). Vertical dashed line. Label handled separately.

Design: points every 1m -> many; use line. Add deviation shading? no.

Bore: build path. For stages:
- pilot: game.path
- ream/pull: full recorded path (game.path)
- prep: maybe no path (just entry stub).
Draw line. If path length<2 return.
Rod ticks: walk along path by distance 3m; compute screen distance and interpolate. Use helper `pointAtDistance`.
Mud dots: use path sampling at every 6m with time offset, draw dots moving toward exit? Skip if low performance. Add small glow.
Sonde rings at head for pilot.
Pits: entry and exit.

Let me add helper `pathScreen`. Also draw entry/exit target markers.

For design path when route skipped: no design (prep.route==='skip'). But in prep stage we need show design after marking. job.designVisible getter? Renderer: `if (game.prep?.route === 'skip' && game.stage !== 'prep')` hide. In prep, show design always once route chosen? If not chosen yet, maybe show faint design as "проект" since contract has it. We can show always in prep to illustrate. But then skipping route has no visual consequence until pilot. Renderer: show design if stage==='prep' || prep.route !== 'skip'. Good.

Exit target always shown.

Utility labels after everything so on top; draw for revealed utilities only within view.

Let's write.

## Objective
- Build “Avto-M Driller HDD 2.0” from the user’s concept: a realistic HDD crew simulator with a construction site, five crew roles, underground cross-section, five work stages, tool choices, and consequences.
- The user then requested changing the in-game currency to US dollars: “Валюта в $”.

## Requirements
- Game must be playable and mobile-friendly with responsive layouts and touch controls.
- Implement five stages: site prep, pilot bore, mud control, reaming, pullback/handover.
- Include five specialists with individual bonuses: operator, locator, mud specialist, mechanic, foreman.
- Show realistic site, crew participation, underground layers, designed vs. actual bore path, existing utilities.
- Tool/mud selection must affect risk and outcome; operator decisions must have consequences.
- Currency must be `$`, not `₽`; economics should be rebalanced for USD rather than only changing the symbol.
- User’s original message was cut off at “Поэтому новую версию 2.0 я”, but intent to build version 2.0 is clear.

## Decisions
- Built as a static HTML/CSS/JS ES-module game served from repository root; no build framework.
- Canvas 2D renderer for site, layered underground cross-section, rig, workers, utilities, bore, reamer, and product pipe.
- Single-page screen flow: title → contracts → optional crew editing → prep → pilot → mud → reaming → pullback → results overlay.
- Persistent progress via `localStorage` key `avto-m-driller-hdd-2`.
- Five prebuilt contracts; all available immediately.
- Crew selection uses 3 candidates per role, salaries deducted per shift, XP/levels persist.
- Failure conditions: 2 utility strikes, 2 frac-outs, or 2 overload events.
- Initial economics were ruble-scale; salaries were reduced once (`38k–52k` → `9k–18k`) but now need full USD rescaling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/data.js`, `src/util.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/app.js`.
- Implemented title screen, contract cards, crew selection, prep checklist/sheets, pilot controls, mud stage, reaming, pullback, pause/exit, help, results, XP and save/load.
- Implemented canvas scene: sky, site, layered soil, grid, utilities, design path, bore, rig, mud/water tanks, truck, trailer, rods, excavator, cones, workers, sonar link, scan/frac effects.
- Added mobile layout CSS, touch hold buttons, keyboard controls.
- Added favicon data URI.
- Visually verified title, contracts, and prep screens using Playwright screenshots.
- Fixed exit pit to extend to exit depth and moved pit rendering before utilities/bore.
- Hid crew name labels in hero demo and non-active roles in prep.
- Moved foreman to `x=8.5` in prep to reduce label clutter.
- Reduced dev server is running on port 3002; Playwright browser installed.

### Active
- Converting all monetary values and displays from `₽` to `$` and rebalancing costs/payouts/salaries to USD.
- Preparing to test prep option sheet and full gameplay flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `fmtMoney` in `src/util.js` to USD formatting, e.g. `$24,500` via `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US')`; update `fmtCompact` too.
2. Rescale all economics by roughly ÷10 and adjust for USD:
   - `START_MONEY` 850000 → 85000.
   - Contract payouts 245000/430000/690000 → 24500/43000/69000.
   - Salaries 9000–18000 → roughly 200–580; suggested values: operator 420/580/260, locator 480/360/200, mud 450/330/240, mechanic 450/320/220, foreman 520/480/280.
   - Prep: georadar 1800, docs 600, laser 1200, manual 400, polymer 2400, bentonite 1200, water 400, reamers 1400/2100/2900, safety 900.
   - Penalties: strike 5500, frac 3800, rod 2200, exit 1500, mud frac 1800, ream overload 4500, pull overload 5000, additive 900, mobilization 2500.
3. Replace hardcoded `₽` and numbers in `index.html`, `src/app.js`, `src/util.js`, `src/data.js`, including toast strings and result/deck labels.
4. Change contract card “Смета” from `т₽` to a `$` value.
5. Retest full flow: prep choices, pilot steering, mud slider, reaming, pullback, results; check desktop and mobile screenshots.
6. Inspect console for runtime errors and fix any visual/functional regressions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/app.js`: game state, Job class, all stage mechanics, screens, UI bindings, results, economic calculations.
- `src/data.js`: roles, candidates/salaries, mud mixes, soils, contracts, payout/reamer costs.
- `src/util.js`: `fmtMoney`, `fmtCompact`, `prepCost`, crew helpers.
- `src/render.js`: canvas renderer, site/cross-section/crew/utilities/tools.
- `styles.css`: full responsive UI, game layout, HUD, decks, overlays.
- `index.html`: screen markup, help modal, static money placeholders.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized engine/alarm/UI sounds.
- `screenshots/title.png`, `screenshots/contracts.png`, `screenshots/prep.png`, `screenshots/prep2.png`, `screenshots/sheet.png`: current visual references.

- Server command used: `PORT=3002 OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=/tmp/opencode node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`; server is running from repo root.
- Playwright is available as `playwright-cli`; browser was installed with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.

219: export function designDepthAt(c, x) {
220:   const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, x / c.length));
221:   const s = t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
222:   const base = c.entryDepth + (c.exitDepth - c.entryDepth) * s;
223:   const amp = Math.max(0.4, c.maxDepth - (c.entryDepth + c.exitDepth) / 2);
224:   return base + Math.pow(Math.sin(Math.PI * t), 1.15) * amp;
225: }
226: 
227: export function buildDesign(c) {
228:   const pts = [];
229:   for (let x = 0; x <= c.length + 0.001; x += 1) {
230:     pts.push({ x, d: designDepthAt(c, x) });
231:   }
232:   return pts;
233: }

235: export function prepareContract(c) {
236:   if (c._ready) return c;
237:   c.design = buildDesign(c);
238:   c.layers = buildLayers(c.soil);
239:   c.utilities = c.utilities.map((u, i) => {
240:     const depth = Math.max(0.8, designDepthAt(c, u.x) + u.offset);
241:     const type = UTILITY_TYPES[u.type];
242:     return {
243:       ...u,
244:       id: `u${i + 1}`,
245:       depth,
246:       label: type.label,
247:       color: type.color,
248:       size: type.size,
249:       clearance: 0.55 + type.size,
250:       hit: false
251:     };
252:   });
253:   c.reamers = makeReamers(c);
254:   c._ready = true;
255:   return c;
256: }

263:     { ratio: 1.7, name: 'Усиленный', hint: 'Больше диаметр скважины, выше нагрузка и риск выхода раствора.' }
264:   ];
265:   return opts.map((o, i) => ({
266:     ...o,

268:     dia: Math.round(base * o.ratio / 10) * 10,
269:     cost: [14000, 21000, 29000][i],
